items.caption:
Even a nap of about six minutes helped recall in one study.
In a 2008 Journal of Sleep Research experiment, volunteers who napped, even about 6 minutes on average, recalled more of a 30-word list an hour later than those who stayed awake. Longer naps did better still.

items.caption:
A week of camping moved body clocks about two hours.
In a 2013 University of Colorado Boulder study, 8 volunteers camped a week in summer with only natural light, and their melatonin rhythm moved about two hours earlier. Small study, summer only.

items.caption:
Vivid dreams, but sleep felt deep.
In a 2026 study, 44 healthy adults in a sleep lab were woken more than 1,000 times from stage 2 non-REM sleep (no rapid eye movements) and asked how deep their sleep had felt: deepest after no experience at all or after vivid, immersive dreams. Depth was self-rated, not measured, and it is one study.
